Your Summary

You were diagnosed with breast cancer in March 2021. You had surgery to remove the cancer from your left breast and nearby lymph nodes, followed by chemotherapy after surgery. In 2023, scans showed that the cancer had spread to your liver and bones. You then started treatment with weekly paclitaxel chemotherapy, which helped control the cancer. More recently, your treatment was changed to ribociclib tablets together with fulvestrant injections. Your latest scans show that the cancer is currently stable.

Your Diagnosis

Metastatic Breast Cancer (Stage IV)

Your diagnosis was confirmed on 15 March 2021.

Your specific type of breast cancer:

Oestrogen receptor positive (ER+)
Your cancer cells have receptors that respond to the hormone oestrogen. This means hormone therapy medicines can be used to help treat your cancer.
Progesterone receptor positive (PR+)
Your cancer cells also respond to the hormone progesterone.
HER2 negative
Your cancer cells have normal levels of the HER2 protein.

Learn more about breast cancer

For trusted information about your diagnosis and what to expect, visit Cancer Research UK - Breast Cancer . You can also read about stages and grades to better understand your results.

Your Treatment

You are currently receiving treatment for your breast cancer. Your care team reviews your treatment regularly to make sure it's working well for you.

Current Treatment
Ribociclib + Fulvestrant
Started 04 November 2024

Ribociclib is a targeted cancer treatment tablet (CDK4/6 inhibitor), and fulvestrant is a hormone therapy injection. These treatments work together to help slow the growth of hormone receptor-positive breast cancer.

You have received 5 different treatments since your diagnosis. See the Treatments tab for full details.

Treatments

Treatment Summary

You received a total of 5 lines of therapy. The treatment regimen included adjuvant chemotherapy with ddAC-T, followed by adjuvant letrozole, then supportive treatment with paclitaxel, letrozole, and finally a combination of ribociclib and fulvestrant. The intent of the treatment was initially curative, but shifted to supportive over time.

04 November 2024

Ribociclib + Fulvestrant

Class: SERD • Intent: Disease control

Schedule: Ribociclib 600mg daily (21 on/7 off) + Fulvestrant 500mg IM q4weeks

View Original Report 
2ND LINE supportive THERAPY - 04/11/2024 REGIMEN: Ribociclib 600mg PO days 1-21 q28days + Fulvestrant 500mg IM q4weeks (loading dose day 1, 15, then monthly) RATIONALE: Progression on AI monotherapy. targeted therapy not previously used. Fulvestrant preferred over AI given prior AI progression.
04 March 2024

Letrozole (maintenance)

Class: hormone therapy • Intent: Disease control

Schedule: 2.5mg daily continuous

View Original Report 
MAINTENANCE ENDOCRINE THERAPY - 04/03/2024 REGIMEN: Letrozole 2.5mg PO daily RATIONALE: Excellent response to chemotherapy. ER+ disease suitable for endocrine maintenance. Plan 3-monthly surveillance CT.
11 September 2023

Paclitaxel weekly

Class: Taxane • Intent: Disease control

Schedule: 80mg/m² weekly x 12 weeks, then maintenance

View Original Report 
1ST LINE supportive CHEMOTHERAPY - 11/09/2023 REGIMEN: Weekly Paclitaxel 80mg/m² SCHEDULE: Weekly x 12 weeks, then reassess RATIONALE: Metastatic recurrence with visceral disease. Taxane rechallenge appropriate >12 months from adjuvant. Aim for rapid disease control before endocrine switch.
01 November 2021

Letrozole (adjuvant)

Class: hormone therapy • Intent: curative

Schedule: 2.5mg daily x 5-10 years

View Original Report 
ADJUVANT ENDOCRINE THERAPY - 01/11/2021 REGIMEN: Letrozole 2.5mg PO daily DURATION: Planned 5-10 years RATIONALE: Post-menopausal, ER+ disease. Extended adjuvant therapy for node-positive disease.
14 June 2021

ddAC-T (Dose-dense AC → Paclitaxel)

Class: Anthracycline + Taxane (adjuvant) • Intent: curative

Schedule: AC q2weeks x 4 cycles → Paclitaxel q2weeks x 4 cycles

View Original Report 
ADJUVANT CHEMOTHERAPY - 14/06/2021 REGIMEN: Dose-dense AC-T - Doxorubicin 60mg/m² + Cyclophosphamide 600mg/m² q2weeks x 4 cycles - Followed by Paclitaxel 175mg/m² q2weeks x 4 cycles - G-CSF support (pegfilgrastim) day 2 each cycle RATIONALE: Node-positive, intermediate Oncotype score. Dose-dense regimen for higher-risk features.

Uncomplicated

Type: Therapeutic • Intent: Curative

View Original Report 
OPERATION NOTE - 10/05/2021 PROCEDURE: Wide local excision left breast upper outer quadrant + sentinel lymph node biopsy ANAESTHESIA: General POSITION: Supine, left arm abducted FINDINGS: - Tumour localised with ultrasound guidance - 3 sentinel lymph nodes identified with blue dye and radiocolloid PROCEDURE: - Skin incision circumareolar extended laterally - Tumour excised with 1cm macroscopic margin - Cavity shaved (superior, inferior, medial, lateral, deep) - Sentinel nodes excised via separate axillary incision - Haemostasis achieved, drains not required - Skin closed with absorbable sutures OPERATIVE TIME: 95 minutes BLOOD LOSS: 50ml COMPLICATIONS: None

Side Effects & Toxicity

Side Effects Summary

You experienced several toxicities throughout treatment, including nausea, neutropenia, alopecia, peripheral neuropathy, arthralgia, and fatigue, with some events reaching grade 2 or higher severity. You's neutropenia worsened over time, reaching grade 3 on one occasion, prompting a hold in treatment. Dose modifications were made, including a reduction in Paclitaxel from 80mg/m² to 65mg/m² and a temporary hold of Ribociclib.

25 November 2024 held

Treatment Held

Associated with: Ribociclib + Fulvestrant
Grade 3 Neutropenia Grade 2 Fatigue

Action: Ribociclib held, restart at 400mg when ANC >1.0

Cycle 1 ribociclib day 21: ANC 0.6 (grade 3 neutropenia). Hold ribociclib. Recheck bloods in 1 week. If ANC >1.0, restart at 400mg. Moderate fatigue - lifestyle advice given.
